lines: Imagine falling from the sky through a violent storm and waking up alone in a deadly jungle.
On 24 December 1971 a passenger plane is struck by lightning and breaks apart midair.
Seventeen year old Juliane Koepcke falls about 3000 meters while still strapped to her seat row.
She wakes up on the dark forest floor with a broken collarbone and a deep arm cut.
She also suffers from a painful eye injury and a severe concussion after the terrifying plunge.
Her biologist father previously taught her that following flowing water always leads back to people.
She finds a tiny creek and begins walking through the dense and dangerous Peruvian rainforest.
Days pass slowly as she follows the winding water toward a larger and safer river.
Up to 14 other passengers survive the initial crash but tragically die before any rescue arrives.
She spends 11 long days completely alone in the unforgiving jungle facing unimaginable odds.
After 9 days of difficult travel she finally discovers a remote lumberjack camp by the river.
She is found by local workers who provide medical help and bring her back to safety.
Juliane remains the only official survivor of LANSA Flight 508 against all odds and expectations.
Would you have the mental strength to survive 11 days alone in the dangerous rainforest?
draft_evening.title: The Girl Who Fell 3000 Meters And Survived

lines: If you get trapped in a blizzard on the highway, do not leave your vehicle behind.
Mark is stranded on a dark interstate as freezing whiteout conditions rapidly bury the road.
Subzero darkness surrounds him, and he must stay alive until morning road crews can arrive.
A violent wall of heavy snow slams into his windshield, killing visibility in every direction.
He decides to stay inside the car because it provides shelter against the lethal wind.
A vehicle is far easier for rescue crews to find than a person walking alone.
One. He steps outside quickly to clear thick snow from the car exhaust pipe first.
A blocked exhaust pipe can rapidly fill the cabin with deadly, invisible carbon monoxide gas.
Two. Mark ties a bright cloth to the car door so search teams spot it.
He also turns on the inside dome light so rescuers can see him through darkness.
Three. He runs the car engine for about 10 minutes each hour to get heat.
He cracks a side window open a little to let fresh outside air circulate through.
He settles into his seat, watching the clock tick down in the dark freezing cabin.
His signals are glowing bright and the interior warmth keeps him safe from the blizzard.
It was the perfect survival plan, but Mark suddenly notices a deadly problem forming outside.
Drifting snow has rapidly piled over the exhaust pipe again while his engine is running.
part1.cliffhanger: A heavy snowdrift has completely sealed the exhaust pipe again while the engine is running, risking carbon monoxide buildup inside the cabin.

lines: Part 2. Heavy snow has completely buried Mark's exhaust pipe, threatening carbon monoxide buildup.
Mark immediately cuts the engine to stop toxic carbon monoxide gas from flooding inside.
He opens his door into the biting wind to inspect the rear bumper area.
One. He quickly pushes away the heavy packed snow clearing the exhaust pipe.
A blocked pipe fills the car cabin with invisible gas in a few minutes.
Two. He steps back inside the shelter and cracks the side window open a little.
Fresh outside air flows inside, keeping the atmosphere inside the car safe and clear.
Three. He runs the engine to get heat for about 10 minutes each hour.
Running the heater constantly wastes precious fuel while Mark waits for morning help.
He double checks that the bright cloth remains tied firmly outside on his door.
The bright cloth gives search teams a visible marker in the blinding white storm.
He keeps the interior dome light turned on so rescue crews spot him easily.
Leaving the car to walk through deep snow puts any driver in grave danger.
Staying inside the car provides shelter and keeps him much easier to locate.
Glowing headlights approach through darkness as snowplow operators finally reach his stranded vehicle.
Mark safe inside waves at the rescue team as they clear a path.
Always stay inside your car during a highway blizzard. Follow for a new scenario tomorrow.
draft_morning.title: Trapped in a Blizzard Part 2: How to Survive a Buried Car
draft_morning.description: Mark faces a deadly exhaust pipe blockage during a night blizzard on the highway. Learn the life-saving steps to avoid carbon monoxide poison and get rescued safely.
